text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've noticed the skin condition on your left dorsal hand and if it's itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned enjoying sunbathing; do you recall if this spot on your left dorsal hand appeared after a specific period of sun exposure, and does it feel raised or flat to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall how long this rough, sandpaper-like plaque has been present, and have you noticed any similar spots on other sun-exposed areas like your face or arms? Given your history of sunbathing, this could be related to cumulative UV damage.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes, Hypertension Social history: Non-smoker, denies alcohol use, enjoys outdoor activities

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Dermoscopy of the left dorsal hand lesion. Given the rough, sandpaper-like texture and your history of sun exposure, I suspect actinic keratosis, so I need a closer look to confirm.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Findings: Hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis, solar elastosis, and atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis. These findings are consistent with actinic keratosis. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Dermatological Inspection: Rough, scaly plaque observed on the left dorsal hand. Palpation: No tenderness or pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis

The biopsy results confirm hyperkeratosis, solar elastosis, and atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis, which are definitive for actinic keratosis. Given your history of sunbathing and the characteristic sandpaper-like texture on your sun-exposed hand, this is the expected diagnosis. We will discuss treatment options to prevent progression to squamous cell carcinoma.
